_comment: Behaviours that were fixed once and must not be silently re-broken.
A permission list cannot protect a fixed behaviour here: `main` waives
REVIEW for the bypass cohort but never waives VALIDATION (see the note in
.github/workflows/ci.yml above the ci-status job). So the durable guard is
a test that runs in the pull-request lane -- it blocks everyone equally,
including every review-bypass user and every --admin merge.
That leaves one hole: a test can be deleted, and a deleted test is green.
This file closes it. Each entry pins the tests that PROVE a behaviour --
the file, the named cases inside it, and an assertion floor. CI fails the
PR when any of those disappear.
Deleting or weakening an entry is deliberately an actor-gated edit: this
file is listed in main.protected_pipeline_paths in config/ci-governance.json,
Assertion floors are set BELOW the current count on purpose. They catch a
test file being gutted, not ordinary edits that add or reshuffle a couple
of assertions. Raise a floor when a behaviour gains real new coverage.

protected_behaviors.name: location-people-search-finds-a-person-from-one-letter
protected_behaviors.summary: Every people picker on the Location surface matches a query that BEGINS a word ahead of one that merely appears inside it, so one typed letter narrows the list. One character keeps only word-beginning matches (falling back to loose ones when nothing begins with it, so it can never empty a list that has a match); two or more characters drop nothing. Combining marks are part of a word, so an Indic name is never split at its matras.
why_it_needs_a_lock: The bug WAS a bare `includes(query)` filter, and it was duplicated at six
call sites: the add-people sheet in Circle detail, the Circle grow sheet
reached from Check-In, the check-in contact list, the map's people tray,
and both recipient searches on the hub. Every branch cut before aa7be6ea2
still carries that one-line filter verbatim in all six, so a conflict
resolved the wrong way silently restores it with nothing in review to
notice -- the list simply stops narrowing again.
The Indic half is the part no reviewer would catch. `/[^\p{L}\p{N}]+/u`
reads a matra as a word separator, so it shredded every Devanagari name
and shipped green past 13 unit tests, typecheck, lint, a full-suite
baseline and a verified UAT deploy, because every fixture was Latin. See
R20 in .claude/skills/safe-changes/SKILL.md. Dropping the \p{M} from that
character class is a one-character edit that no Latin test can fail.

required_titles: narrows to the person whose name begins with a single typed letter
keeps every match beyond one character, word beginnings first
never empties a list that has a match, even for one character
keeps an Indic name whole instead of splitting it at every matra
still finds an Indic name by a syllable inside it
finds a connection from the first letter here too
paints its blocked Select people CTA the same as the Circle detail copy
finds a connection from the first letter of any of their names
blocks Create only while the name is empty, and says so visibly

at merge commit 7c647f75e, and was resolved correctly only by hand.

shows every match for a single typed letter

protected_behaviors.name: connect-request-asks-before-it-shares
protected_behaviors.summary: A connection request opens the capability review pre-granting nothing in either direction. The only permitted bypass is a catalog that is empty on BOTH sides, and it must send empty handle lists.
why_it_needs_a_lock: This contract test sat RED on main from 2026-08-15 to 2026-08-16 and
nobody saw it, because ci.yml has no vitest lane and the full suite only
runs in the merge queue -- which every review-bypass user skips. It was
asserting dialog copy, so ordinary UI polish made it stale; it now
asserts the consent shape instead, which is the part that must not move.

required_titles: requires an explicit capability review whenever there is anything to review

protected_behaviors.name: connect-rias-tab-lists-only-verified-advisers
protected_behaviors.summary: The RIAs tab shows only connections the server has annotated as verified RIAs, and the heading count, the empty state and the rows all read that one filtered list. A connection carrying no annotation is NOT an adviser.
why_it_needs_a_lock: The directory half of this tab was audience-split server-side from the
start; the 'My connections' list above it was never split at all, so the
RIAs tab repeated the People tab exactly and listed people who had never
finished RIA onboarding. A tester found it, not CI.
The filter is one clause on a useMemo and the annotation is one key on a
dict two repos apart. Either can be dropped in a conflict resolution with
nothing in review to notice -- the tab simply goes back to listing
everyone, which looks like a populated tab rather than a broken one.
The fail-closed direction matters as much as the filter: an unannotated
row must be hidden from the tab, never promoted into it.

required_titles: lists only verified advisers under My connections on the RIAs tab
treats a connection with no RIA annotation as not an adviser
test_list_connections_annotates_ria_status_per_row
test_list_connections_uses_the_same_verified_gate_as_the_directory

protected_behaviors.name: one-location-duration-states-itself-once
protected_behaviors.summary: Choosing the open-ended share duration collapses the timed wheel instead of fading it behind a second, contradicting label; and the Request lane never offers an open-ended option at all, because you cannot ask to watch someone until THEY stop.
why_it_needs_a_lock: The faded remains of the wheel WERE the defect: the chip stating the
choice was a child of an opacity-40 wrapper, so it rendered grey in the
middle of a grey control while a blue button under it said the opposite
words. Restoring the fade is a one-line change.
The Request half is worse than cosmetic. `allowUntilStop={false}` is a
single prop with no test on either half before this entry, and the value
it suppresses is a non-numeric sentinel that this lane later runs
Number() over -- deleting the prop posts NaN to a `gt=0` field.

required_titles: emits the until-stop alias and removes the wheel while toggled on
recovers a sentinel value into a real duration on a lane that hides the option
never offers an open-ended duration when asking someone else

protected_behaviors.name: one-location-share-picker-says-who-can-already-see-you
protected_behaviors.summary: The share recipient picker separates people who already hold an active grant into their own group, showing the same remaining time the Active shares screen shows for that grant. The grouping appears only when there is something to group.
why_it_needs_a_lock: Picking someone who already holds an active grant does not extend it --
`_create_enforced_grant_row` revokes the old row and inserts a new one --
so a re-pick silently restarts a running timer. Before this, every row
looked identical, so that was invisible at the moment of choosing.
The whole feature is one read of `vm.activeOwnerGrants`, a field that sat
on the same view-model unread for the life of the screen. Dropping the
read returns the picker to a flat list that looks correct.

required_titles: separates people who can already see you from people who cannot
keeps one flat list when nobody can see you yet

protected_behaviors.name: one-location-onboarding-art-is-not-positioned-from-the-viewport
protected_behaviors.summary: The Check-in card's artwork is anchored in a percentage of its own region, so its place inside the card does not change when the viewport height changes. The copy and the artwork never overlap.
why_it_needs_a_lock: This shipped as five separate `bottom` rules on [data-one-checkin-art] --
two `vh` clamps and three fixed pixel values inside width/height media
queries -- each of which outranks the element's own class by source order.
The card's size is width-driven and never moved; the art slid up inside it
as the phone got taller, until it ran over the body copy. A tester found it
by stepping from a 393x852 iPhone 14 Pro to a 430x932 Pro Max.
A width-only sweep cannot catch this, and neither can reading the source:
the first attempt at this fix removed ONE clamp and the browser test found
four more overrides still winning. The lock is the height sweep.

required_titles: the artwork is not positioned from the viewport

protected_behaviors.name: gemini-endpoint-select-matches-the-key-field-on-webkit
protected_behaviors.summary: The API endpoint picker and the key field under it share a radius, height and text inset — including under WebKit, where a native <select> ignores author border-radius unless appearance is removed.
why_it_needs_a_lock: `appearance-none` looks like a cosmetic class and is the entire fix. Under
WebKit's default `appearance: menulist` the engine draws the control and
overrides the author's border-radius: measured 5px against the input's
14px, before AND after handing the select the input's classes.
Chromium honours the author radius either way, so a Chromium-only test
passes the broken control. The iOS app is a WKWebView. Deleting the class,
or letting this spec fall out of the webkit project's testMatch, silently
restores the defect on the platform most of our users are on.

required_titles: appearance-none is load-bearing, not decoration

protected_behaviors.name: location-header-status-names-what-the-switch-controls
protected_behaviors.summary: The Location header's status always reads "Location on/off/paused/blocked/limited" at every width, and renders under the title rather than beside the switch.
why_it_needs_a_lock: The full string beside the switch wrapped the 28px title on every iPhone,
so it was shortened to one word on phones. That fit, and it cost the label
its meaning: iOS showed a bare green switch over the word "On", which
never said what it switched. Reported from the device.
The one-word form is the tempting fix every time the title wraps again.
Moving the status under the title is what makes the full string affordable;
putting it back in the actions column brings the abbreviation back with it.

required_titles: keeps the status card and location toggle grouped as one control
names what the switch controls in every state, at every width

protected_behaviors.name: confirming-a-place-in-onboarding-turns-location-on
protected_behaviors.summary: Saving and labelling a place during Location onboarding sets the live preview on, so the hub the person is redirected to does not greet them with "Location off" seconds after they granted permission and dropped a pin.
why_it_needs_a_lock: Onboarding captures a position DIRECTLY rather than through
`ensureForegroundLocationReady`, so it never reaches `activateMyLocation`
and never sets `selfPreviewEnabled`. A new owner also has no grants and no
nearby presence, so all three disjuncts behind `locationEnabled` are false.
It shipped because every hub test reaches the hub through
`skipLocationEntryFlow`, which presses "Skip for now" on the save modal —
so the save path never once reached an assertion about the header. The
guard has to be a test that SAVES.
The write is two fields on the same call the header switch itself uses.
Deleting it restores a hub that contradicts what the person just did.

required_titles: turns location on once a place is confirmed in onboarding

protected_behaviors.name: duration-cells-stay-compact-wherever-they-render
protected_behaviors.summary: Every duration choice in Location renders at the 44px / 15px cell, including the nearby Check-in sheet's "Stay visible for" pills, which now reuse the ladder's exported class strings instead of a morphy Button.
why_it_needs_a_lock: A morphy <Button> at size="default" is 50px tall with a 17px label, and
neither can be overridden from outside: min-h-[50px] sits in a different
tailwind-merge group from h-*, and .ui-text-button-label forces 17px
!important. So the Check-in sheet rendered the SAME role 6px taller and 2px
larger than this app's own duration control, and the only way back is a raw
<button> carrying the ladder's classes.
Reaching for <Button> while tidying this sheet is the obvious move and it
silently undoes the fix. The geometry test is what catches that.

required_titles: Check-in duration pills reuse the ladder cell

protected_behaviors.name: onboarding-is-a-one-way-funnel
protected_behaviors.summary: One resolver decides which onboarding step somebody is on, and nothing renders an onboarding surface until every input it needs is known. A person who finished the funnel can never reach sign-in, phone verification or the setup hub again by any arrival path, and the lock screen and the phone screen can never be on screen at the same time.
why_it_needs_a_lock: The bug WAS three guards each resolving their own copy of the same
state and each redirecting on its own schedule. That shape produced
three separate user-visible defects, and every one of them comes back
the moment a guard starts fetching for itself again: a screen rendered
from a default value and replaced a tick later, two guards deciding at
once, and an onboarding route no guard claimed.
The lock surface is a portal painted at z-712 over an opaque backdrop.
It does not need to share a subtree with the phone screen to cover it,
so no amount of guard nesting keeps the two apart on its own -- only an
explicit check against the winning step does. Someone re-nesting a
guard, or mounting the lock dialog from a new route, reintroduces the
collision with nothing in review to notice.
The Back defect had no guard at all: /register-phone is exempt from the
setup gate and outside /one, so nothing ejected an already-verified
person who arrived there. Adding a route to the funnel without adding
it to ONBOARDING_ROUTES silently opens that door again.

protected_behaviors.name: one-location-emergency-control-is-labelled-sms
protected_behaviors.summary: The emergency control reads "SMS" on every surface a person meets it: the hold button on the Emergency help screen, and the Home hub quick-action tile. The screen description names the same word the button shows.
why_it_needs_a_lock: This label flipped twice in two days -- SMS -> SOS on 2026-08-18 across
three commits (bc3dd4694, fd73a42b1, 9644f1926), then back to SMS on
2026-08-19 -- and neither direction was caught by anything.
The reason it was free to drift is that sos-panel.test.tsx, the one suite
that asserts the glyph, was in NO pack in web-targeted-check.sh. The
directory regex on line 133 matches components/one-location/, so a PR
touching this file looked covered and the lane went green, while the npm
script that lane fires enumerated 8 files and never included this one.
Every identifier underneath still says sos (data-testid, event name,
voice control id one-location-action-sos, backend enum), so a grep for
'sos' does not tell you what the screen says. Only these assertions do.

required_titles: shows 'Stop sharing' only while a session is active and calls onStopSos
returns the core to SMS once the session is no longer active (external revoke sync)
resolves a fresh local emergency number as Save My Soul opens

protected_behaviors.name: your-map-consent-button-is-never-a-silent-no-op
protected_behaviors.summary: The renderer-consent card on Your Map (and on the check-in route, which mounts the same component) always answers a tap. With a lock it writes the current consent version and the card goes; with no lock it asks for the lock instead of offering a Continue it cannot complete; while the write is in flight it is busy, so one decision sends one request; and a map-state read that started before the write can never revive the card the owner already dismissed.
why_it_needs_a_lock: The bug WAS `if (!vaultOwnerToken) return;` as the first line of
acceptRenderer, and it shipped from the day the handler was written
(84d0b1000, 2026-07-23, PR #4650) to 2026-08-19 without one test ever
reaching it -- because the suite's vault mock was a hardcoded truthy
token with no way for a case to vary it. VaultLockGuard renders /one
children with a NULL token on purpose when the account has no lock
(`if (hasVault === false) return children`), so that state is not
theoretical: a UAT session opened /one/location/map at 18:15:50Z on
2026-08-19 and produced neither the token-gated map-state read nor a
map-preferences PATCH. The whole screen -- markers, people tray, the
Sharing count and every part of Nearby Check-In -- sits behind that one
button, so a silent return there takes the entire surface down while
leaving it looking completely alive.
Delete the falsy-token case and the screen can go back to doing nothing
with nothing said, and no other test in the repository would notice: the
map suite and the vault-guard suite live in different targeted packs, so
the seam this bug lives in is covered by neither.

required_titles: writes the current consent version and dismisses the card
asks for the missing lock instead of doing nothing when there is no owner token
sends one write for a double tap
never lets a map-state read that started earlier revive the dismissed card
